articles.title: Spanish Hotel Operator Buys Chemists’ Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street for $95M
articles.narrative: Eurostars Hotel Company, a Spanish hotel chain, has acquired the 107-key Chemists' Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street in Midtown Manhattan for approximately $95 million from Azora. The transaction marks a return of the property to its previous ownership roots, as Eurostars is a subsidiary of Grupo Hotusa, which previously owned the hotel. The historic 14-story building, originally constructed around 1910 as the headquarters for the Chemists' Club, was redeveloped into a hotel in 1997 and recently underwent a significant redesign and rebranding.

data_points.address: 52 East 41st Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: The 14-story building was originally the headquarters of the Chemists' Club and features a ground-floor steakhouse, lounge bar, coworking spaces, and a fitness center.
data_points.project_notes: The property was previously acquired in 2007 for $77 million by Grupo Hotusa and Losan Hotels. It was redeveloped in 1997 and opened as the Dylan Hotel in 2000, then heavily redesigned and rebranded as the Chemists' Club Hotel last year.

articles.title: Izo Capital Lends $26M on Wyoming Apartments Near Jackson Hole
articles.narrative: Sundance Properties secured $25.6 million in construction financing from Izo Capital for the completion of Phase 1 of its Flats at Alpine Junction multifamily development in Alpine, WY. The loan will fund the construction of 48 additional units, bringing the first phase to 64 units, with 16 units already completed and leased. The project is strategically located near Jackson Hole, addressing a critical need for attainable rental housing in a supply-constrained market with high home prices and strong demand drivers, including a new medical center and a charter school.

data_points.notable_features: Located 35 miles from Jackson Hole mountain valley with direct access to the START Bus system connecting Alpine and Jackson. Benefits from local demand drivers including a newly opened medical center and a public charter school.
data_points.project_notes: The loan is a 24-month senior construction loan to fund the completion of Phase 1, which includes three additional buildings comprising 48 apartments. The first phase is slated for completion in spring 2027.

articles.market_intelligence: Median home prices in Jackson Hole are close to $3 million, with townhomes starting at around $1 million, indicating a strong demand for more attainable rental housing. Izo Capital is on pace to close around $150 million of loans in 2026, largely focused on multifamily deals in supply-constrained markets, with a focus on stretch construction loans covering up to 80-85% of development costs combined with a preferred equity piece.

articles.title: CW Realty Closes Deal to Buy 55 Smith Street in Downtown Brooklyn for $58M
articles.narrative: CW Realty Group has acquired a significant development site at 55 Smith Street in Downtown Brooklyn from Edison Properties for $58 million. The 13,707-square-foot parcel, also known as 160 Livingston Street, is considered one of the largest residential development opportunities in the area. The site offers substantial development potential, allowing for up to 137,000 square feet as-of-right or 164,000 square feet under the Universal Affordability Preference program, with no height or parking restrictions for a potential housing development. Brokers noted the strong demand for well-located development sites in New York City, particularly in neighborhoods with robust residential fundamentals and supportive zoning.

data_points.notable_features: One of the biggest residential development opportunities in Downtown Brooklyn, with flexible zoning allowing for significant housing development.
data_points.project_notes: Developers can build 137,000 square feet as-of-right or 164,000 square feet under the Universal Affordability Preference program, with no height limits or parking requirements. Development is not restricted to rental housing or condominiums.

articles.title: Kimco Buys Two Broward Retail Centers for $109M
articles.narrative: Kimco Realty, a prominent owner of grocery-anchored retail centers, has acquired two retail properties in Broward County, Florida, from KPR Centers for a total of $109 million. The acquisition includes Sunshine Plaza in Tamarac for $56 million and Pompano Marketplace in Pompano Beach for $53 million. Both properties are significant retail hubs anchored by major grocery and discount retailers, reinforcing Kimco's presence in the South Florida market.

data_points.notable_features: Both properties are grocery-anchored retail centers.
data_points.project_notes: KPR Centers previously acquired Sunshine Plaza for $28.5 million in 2014 and Pompano Marketplace for $46.8 million in 2015.

articles.title: IPA Negotiates Sale of 306-Unit Apartment Community in Red Oak, Texas
articles.narrative: Institutional Property Advisors (IPA) has facilitated the sale of Emerson at Red Oak, a 306-unit apartment community located in Red Oak, a southern suburb of Dallas. The transaction involved CESM Real Estate as the seller and Professional Equity Management as the buyer. The property, built in 2023, features a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom units and a variety of amenities.

data_points.address: 351 Hickory Creek Dr, Red Oak, TX
data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool, fitness center, picnic and grilling areas, dog park, game room, and a business center.

articles.title: Hanover, TIG Complete 213,425 SF Spec Industrial Project in South Houston
articles.narrative: A partnership between Hanover Co. and Transwestern Investment Group (TIG) has completed Kirby 288, a 213,425-square-foot speculative industrial project in South Houston. The development, which began construction in August 2025, features a cross-dock configuration, 36-foot clear heights, and excess trailer storage. Colliers is handling the leasing for the new facility.

data_points.notable_features: Cross-dock configuration, 36-foot clear heights, and excess trailer storage.

articles.title: JLL Brokers Sale of 113,823 SF Shopping Center in North Dallas
articles.narrative: JLL has brokered the sale of Pavilion on Lovers Lane, a 113,823-square-foot shopping center in North Dallas. The two-building center, originally built in 1986 and renovated in 2023, was 99 percent leased at the time of sale. JLL also arranged acquisition financing for the undisclosed buyer.

data_points.notable_features: Two-building center expanded in 2006 and renovated in 2023.

articles.title: Mega Furniture Signs 52,677 SF Retail Lease in Corpus Christi, Texas
articles.narrative: Mega Furniture has signed a 52,677-square-foot retail lease in Corpus Christi, Texas. The property, originally built in 1973, was formerly occupied by another home goods retailer. Cravey Real Estate Services represented the landlord, while Asterra Properties represented the tenant in the transaction.

data_points.address: 4818 S. Padre Island Drive, Corpus Christi, TX

articles.title: CBRE Arranges $30.7M Loan for Refinancing of Apartment Building in West Caldwell, New Jersey
articles.narrative: CBRE has secured a $30.7 million refinancing loan for The Vail, a 92-unit apartment building in West Caldwell, New Jersey. The loan was provided by Principal Financial to the borrower, Accordia. The property offers a mix of studio, one-, and two-bedroom units, with 20% designated as affordable housing.

data_points.notable_features: 20% of units are reserved as affordable housing; units include washers/dryers and select units have private balconies. Amenities include a fitness center, community room, and coworking spaces.

articles.title: Oxford Partners negotiates 20,046-square-foot lease renewal in Houston
articles.narrative: M&C Pump Americas LLC renewed its lease for 20,046 square feet at 15360 Vantage Pkwy W in Houston, Texas. Oxford Partners represented the tenant in the transaction, while JLL represented the landlord, Old House Capital.

articles.title: BGO, Yukon Real Estate Partners sell 291,000-square-foot cold storage warehouse in Kansas
articles.narrative: BGO and Yukon Real Estate Partners have sold the New Century Cold Storage facility, a recently constructed 291,000-square-foot cold storage warehouse in New Century, Kansas, to a client of MetLife Investment Management. The facility was developed as a build-to-suit for a major logistics provider and features direct rail access and strategic proximity to Interstate 35, enhancing its distribution capabilities.

data_points.notable_features: Plant-attached, rail-served cold storage warehouse with direct rail spur to the building and access to BNSF Railway transcontinental intermodal facility. Located within Johnson County Airport Commission’s New Century AirCenter industrial park, less than four miles from Interstate 35.
data_points.project_notes: Purpose-built as a build-to-suit warehouse for CJ Logistics America.

articles.title: Opus begins construction on new high school for Des Moines Christian School
articles.narrative: Opus has commenced construction on a new 133,670-square-foot high school for Des Moines Christian School in Urbandale, Iowa. The facility, located on a 104-acre site acquired by the school in 2024, is a key component of the school's 'Build Today | Plan for Tomorrow' campaign, designed to enhance the student experience. The new high school will feature a two-story academic wing with 24 classrooms and three labs, a collegiate-sized gymnasium, and dedicated spaces for wellness, fine arts, and student activities.

data_points.property_name: Des Moines Christian School High School
data_points.notable_features: Features a two-story academic wing with 24 classrooms and three labs, including STEM spaces, and a gymnasium with seating for over 2,000 fans.
data_points.project_notes: The 104-acre site was purchased in 2024. The project is part of the school's 'Build Today | Plan for Tomorrow' campaign.

articles.title: CrestMarc, Midloch acquire 294-unit apartment property near Sam Houston State University
articles.narrative: CrestMarc and Midloch Investment Partners have acquired The Forum at Sam Houston, a 294-unit apartment property in Huntsville, Texas, catering to the Sam Houston State University community. The property, built in 2010, offers a mix of unit types and amenities, and is strategically located near the university. The acquisition is supported by the university's stable and growing student population and a lack of new competitive developments in the submarket, which is expected to drive sustained leasing strength and rent growth.

data_points.notable_features: Located 0.4 miles from Sam Houston State University; features a resort-style pool, sand volleyball court, basketball court, 24-hour clubhouse, fitness center, bark park, and private shuttle to campus.

articles.market_intelligence: Sam Houston State University has an enrollment of approximately 21,000 students. No new competitive purpose-built developments are currently planned in the submarket.

articles.title: Carlson Partners helps bring Salvation Army store to Edina
articles.narrative: The Salvation Army has secured a new 27,495-square-foot retail lease in Edina, Minnesota, for a new Family Store. This transaction follows a 13-month effort to amend a city code that previously restricted the size of secondhand retail stores, which was unanimously approved by the Edina City Council. The new store will convert an underutilized industrial and flex building into retail and donation processing space, creating approximately 36 jobs.

data_points.notable_features: Converts an underutilized industrial and flex building; includes 18,425 SF of retail and 9,434 SF for donation intake and processing.
data_points.project_notes: Required a 13-month effort to amend a city code prohibiting secondhand retail stores larger than 2,500 SF.

AI Tech Firm Treeswift Signs Four-Year Lease for New Manhattan Headquarters
articles.narrative: Treeswift Inc., an AI-powered infrastructure technology company, has signed a four-year lease for 7,487 square feet at 256 W. 38th St. in Midtown Manhattan, relocating its New York headquarters. The move reflects a broader trend among growing AI companies seeking efficient, well-connected headquarters that foster collaboration and attract talent, rather than exclusively targeting trophy towers.

articles.title: Van Nuys Apartments Trade for First Time Since Delivery
articles.narrative: A 30-unit multifamily property in Van Nuys, CA, has been sold for $9.5 million, marking its first transaction since its construction in 2013. The sale, which garnered significant investor interest due to the property's newer vintage and exemption from the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, was financed with a $6.223 million acquisition loan. The transaction highlights the ongoing demand for well-located multifamily assets in the area.

data_points.notable_features: Newer-vintage multifamily property not subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance.

articles.financing: Acquisition financing of $6,223,000 secured with a five-year loan at 67% loan-to-value, competitive interest rate, and 30-year amortization period.

articles.title: Williamsburg Mixed-Use Sale Completes “Round Trip” for Seller
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of two mixed-use buildings in Brooklyn's Williamsburg neighborhood for $16.4 million. The transaction represents a successful "round trip" for the seller, who had previously acquired the property in 2021 for $12.3 million. The buyer utilized a 1031 exchange to complete the acquisition of the turnkey property, which is situated on the prominent Kent Avenue corridor.

data_points.project_notes: The seller previously acquired the property for $12.3 million in 2021. The buyer completed a 1031 exchange.

articles.title: Locally Based Investors Acquire Encinitas Offices from Family Trust
articles.narrative: Locally based investors DMJ Capital Partners, LLC and StoneSteps Real Estate, LLC have acquired a 40,270-square-foot multi-tenant office property in Encinitas, CA, for $13.5 million. The property, located at 169 Saxony Rd., was previously owned by a family trust for over 24 years. The sale reflects strong investor demand for well-located office assets in the San Diego market, according to the seller's broker.

data_points.project_notes: Property was held in a family trust and owned/operated by the seller and her late father for over 24 years.

articles.title: Treasuries Hover Around 4.7% As Wall Street Questions If Warsh Is A 'Dove In Hawk's Clothing'
articles.narrative: Treasury yields are rising again, with the 10-year note flirting with 4.75%, a level many in commercial real estate had considered a ceiling for debt trouble. This increase follows the Federal Open Market Committee's decision to hold interest rates flat for the fifth consecutive meeting, coupled with new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's comments that have left investors questioning the Fed's commitment to taming inflation. Analysts suggest Warsh's remarks created uncertainty regarding the Fed's strategy for price stability, leading to concerns about the central bank's credibility. This perceived lack of resolve could further drive up longer-dated Treasury yields, directly impacting borrowing costs for commercial real estate debt, and has already coincided with a significant uptick in CMBS delinquencies.

people.name: Krishna Guha
people.title: Head of Central Banking Strategy and Economics

articles.market_intelligence: Yields on 10-year Treasury notes edged up 4 basis points between the Fed's decision and market close on Wednesday, flirting with 4.75% on Friday. CMBS delinquencies ticked up 51 basis points to 7.86% in July, a significant shift from the prior 12 months of stability. The core personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation metric, was 3.4% in May and 3.3% in June.

articles.title: Avison Young Had Assets Frozen By Bank Over Unpaid Taxes
articles.narrative: Avison Young's UK accounts were frozen by NatWest Group due to unpaid taxes, prompting a winding-up petition from His Majesty's Revenue and Customs. A judge ordered the unfreezing of assets, allowing Avison Young to pay its outstanding tax obligations. The brokerage has faced ongoing cash flow issues since 2022, exacerbated by declining real estate deal volumes and a lawsuit from ICG over alleged negligent valuations.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Companies Reshaping Dublin Office Demand As OpenAI Confirms HQ
articles.narrative: OpenAI has leased 88,000 square feet at the Tropical Fruit Warehouse in Dublin, Ireland, for its new European headquarters, with plans to create 250 new roles over the next two years. This move signifies Dublin's growing importance as a hub for global innovation and technology, particularly for artificial intelligence companies. The transaction follows a trend of AI firms establishing significant operational bases in the city, contributing to declining office vacancy rates and rising prime rents.

data_points.project_notes: OpenAI previously occupied coworking space in Dublin and initially took space earmarked for TikTok before TikTok vacated in late 2024.

people.name: Emma Redmond
people.title: Associate General Counsel and Head of Ireland

articles.market_intelligence: Dublin's office vacancy has fallen for five consecutive quarters, reaching 12.2% overall and 9.8% in Dublin 2. Top-tier space vacancy is 5.2%. The current office pipeline is 910,000 SF, the lowest since 2010. Prime rents are around €65 per SF and could reach €70-€80 per SF in the next 6-12 months. A Savills analysis suggests every €1B of generative AI venture capital raised translates to approximately 43,000 SF of additional office demand in San Francisco, potentially leading to 755,000 SF of demand from European-headquartered AI companies by mid-2028.

articles.title: Camden Property Trust Sells West Coast Portfolio, Clears $1.5B Target
articles.narrative: Camden Property Trust has successfully divested its entire 11-property multifamily portfolio in California for $1.63 billion, achieving its strategic goal to exit the state. The Houston-based REIT sold the 3,620-unit portfolio, which spans the Los Angeles-Orange County and San Diego-Inland Empire markets, at approximately $450,000 per unit. The proceeds will be utilized to reduce debt, repurchase shares, and facilitate new investments in Sun Belt growth markets through 1031 exchanges, aligning with the company's strategy to mitigate regulatory costs associated with operating in California.

data_points.project_notes: The portfolio was initially marketed for sale in January for an asking price of approximately $1.5 billion.

articles.market_intelligence: Camden Property Trust's California portfolio's annual NOI would have been reduced by approximately 80 basis points due to regulatory costs. In Q1 2026, over 4,000 new multifamily units broke ground in Los Angeles, the highest since 2022.

articles.title: Churchill Downs Plans To Sell 9 Casinos, Focus On Horse Racing
articles.narrative: Churchill Downs Inc. is divesting nine casino properties across seven states, including Florida, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, Mississippi, New York, and Pennsylvania, to sharpen its focus on horse racing operations and its online betting platform, TwinSpires. The company has engaged Macquarie Capital to manage the sale of these assets. Proceeds from the sales are earmarked for debt reduction, strategic reinvestment in its core racing properties like Churchill Downs Racetrack, and share repurchases. This strategic shift follows a nearly 7% drop in the company's stock price to a six-year low.

data_points.notable_features: Properties include Calder Casino in Florida, Terre Haute Casino in Indiana, and a Hard Rock Casino in Iowa.
data_points.project_notes: Churchill Downs is also undertaking several capital projects, including the $280M-$300M Victory Run development at Churchill Downs Racetrack, set to debut in 2028, and expansions to the Homestretch Club and infield for the 2027 Kentucky Derby.
